question: Who among the following was also known as the Frontier Gandhi?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Abdul Ghaffar Khan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Abdul Ghaffar Khan, also known as Bacha Khan, was a prominent freedom fighter and a devout follower of Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• He earned the title "Frontier Gandhi" due to his leadership in the non-violent resistance movement against British rule in the North-West Frontier Province (now in Pakistan).
 
• He founded the Khudai Khidmatgar ("Servants of God") movement, which advocated for non-violence and social reform.
 
• Abdul Ghaffar Khan was awarded the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award, in 1987.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Khudai Khidmatgar Movement:**

 
 
• Founded by Abdul Ghaffar Khan in 1929, the movement was based on the principles of non-violence and aimed at social reform.
 
• The members, often dressed in red shirts, were also known as "Red Shirts" and were committed to fighting British colonial rule through peaceful means.
 
 
 
• **Non-violent Resistance:**
 
 
• Abdul Ghaffar Khan was a staunch advocate of non-violent resistance, much like Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• His commitment to non-violence was rooted in his belief in Islamic principles and the teachings of the Quran.
 
 
 
• **Political Career:**
 
 
• He was a close ally of the Indian National Congress and worked closely with other prominent leaders of the Indian independence movement.
 
• Despite his efforts for a united India, he faced opposition from the Muslim League and was eventually imprisoned multiple times by the British authorities.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• Abdul Ghaffar Khan's legacy is remembered for his unwavering commitment to peace and non-violence.
 
• He remains a symbol of the power of non-violent resistance and is celebrated for his contributions to India's struggle for independence.
